Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:10:1.hebrew: בשלמא רבה - דאמר שינויא ארומיא דמתניתין דגיטין אמתני' דנזיקין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:10:1.english: Granted, Rabba - Who stated [his] answer regarding the contradiction between the Mishnah of Gittin and the Mishnah of Nezikin.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:10:2.hebrew: לא אמר כר' זירא - דרמא מתני' אברייתא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:10:2.english: Does not say like Rabbi Zeira - Who contrasted the Mishnah with a baraita.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:10:3.hebrew: דמתניתין אלימא ליה לאקשויי - משום דהיא עיקר, ויש תימה כשסותרות זו את זו, וצריך לחזר שיתיישבו. דאילו ברייתא, יש לומר אינה עיקר — רבי לא שנאה, רבי חייא מניין לו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:10:3.english: For a Mishnah is stronger for him to raise a difficulty - Because it is primary, and it is astonishing when [Mishnayot] contradict one another, and one must strive so that they be reconciled. Whereas [with] a baraita, one can say it is not primary — [if] Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] did not teach it, from where [did] Rabbi Chiya [have] it?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:11:1.hebrew: ולעולם כדקיימא לן כשנמצא לאלתר - ואם לאו, פסול, שמא אינו של זה. אבל ברייתא ליכא לשנויי הכי, דכיון דתנא בהדיא "יחזיר לאשה", הוה ליה לפלוגי בין לאלתר בין לזמן מרובה; דלא דמיא למתניתין, דהתם "לא יחזיר" תנא, ומדוקיא הוה דייק "יחזיר" היכא דאמר "תנו", וכיון דלא תנא "יחזיר", לא הוה ליה לפלוגי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:11:1.english: And actually, [it is] as we maintain, when it is found immediately - And if not, [it is] invalid, lest it is not this [person's]. However, [regarding] the baraita, one cannot answer thus, for since it explicitly taught "he shall return [it] to the woman," it should have distinguished between immediately and after a long time. For it is not similar to our Mishnah, as there it taught "he shall not return [it]," and it is from an inference that one deduced "he shall return [it]" where he said "give"; and since it did not teach "he shall return [it]," it did not have to distinguish.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:14:1.english: Where it was found outside - Where caravans are not common.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:15:1.hebrew: ר' ירמיה אמר - הא דקתני יחזיר, כגון דאמרי עדים החתומין בו: מעולם לא חתמנו כו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:15:1.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said - That which it teaches, "he shall return [it]," [refers to] a case where the witnesses signed on it say: "We have never signed, etc."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:18:1.hebrew: ודוקא בצד אות פלונית - דהוה ליה סימן מובהק, ואפילו אם תימצי לומר גבי חזרת אבידה בסימנין — דאיבעיא לן לקמן (בבא מציעא דף כז.) דאורייתא או דרבנן — אפילו פשטת סימנין דרבנן, יש לסמוך על סימן מובהק כזה למשרי אשת איש דאורייתא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:18:1.english: And specifically next to such-and-such a letter - Because it is a clear-cut distinguishing mark; and even if you should say regarding returning a lost item by distinguishing marks — concerning which we raised a dilemma later (Bava Metzia 27a) [whether they are] by Torah law or by rabbinic law — even if you resolve [that] distinguishing marks [are] by rabbinic law, one may rely on a clear-cut distinguishing mark such as this to permit a married woman [which is a matter of] Torah law.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:19:1.hebrew: מספקא ליה לרב אשי סימנין - שמחזירין בהן אבידה, אי דאורייתא היא, ואפילו באיסור דאורייתא סמכינן אסימן כל דהו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:19:1.english: Rav Ashi is uncertain [regarding] distinguishing marks - by which a lost item is returned, whether it is by Torah law, and even in a Torah prohibition we rely on any distinguishing mark whatsoever.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:19:2.hebrew: אי דרבנן - ודוקא באבידה, שהפקר ב"ד הפקר, אבל במידי דאיסורא לא סמכינן. ואי קשיא: נימא הכי קסבר סימנין דרבנן, ונפשוט בעיין דלקמן? לאו פירכא היא, דמנלן דפשיטא ליה? אי נמי מספקא ליה, אית עליה למיסר מספיקא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:19:2.english: Whether [it is] by rabbinic law - And [this applies] specifically to a lost item, for that which is declared ownerless by the court is ownerless; however, in a matter of [ritual] prohibition we do not rely [on them]. And if it is difficult [to you]: let us say he holds thus, [that] distinguishing marks are by rabbinic law, and let us resolve our dilemma below? It is not a difficulty, for how do we know that it is certain to him? Even if he is in doubt about it, it is incumbent upon him to forbid [it] out of doubt.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:1:1.hebrew: חיישינן לשני שוירי - אע"פ שבא אחד לפנינו ואמר "ממני נפל, ופלוני היה משלחו לאשתו", ויודעין אנו שאין שם בשוירי שני אנשים ששמותיהן שוין — חיישינן שמא שוירי אחרת יש, ויש בה יוסף בן שמעון אחר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:1:1.english: We are concerned about two [cities named] Sheviri - Even though someone came before us and said, "It fell from me, and so-and-so was sending it to his wife," and we know that there are not two men in Sheviri whose names are the same, we are concerned that perhaps there is another Sheviri, and there is another Yosef ben Shimon in it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:1:2.hebrew: ואמר ליה רב חסדא לרבה - גרסינן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:1:2.english: And Rav Ḥisda said to Rabba - [This is] our reading.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:1:3.hebrew: כל מעשה ב"ד הרי זה יחזיר - כל מילתא דאתא לב"ד לקיים, דליכא למיחש לנמלך עליהן שלא ליתנן, הרי זה יחזיר. וזה מקוים בב"ד היה, ולכך הובא שם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:1:3.english: Any court enactment must be returned - Any matter that comes to the court to be authenticated, where there is no concern that [the sender] reconsidered regarding them not to give them, must be returned. And this [bill of divorce] had been authenticated in the court, and for that reason it was brought there.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:3:1.hebrew: כשמעתיה - דבעינן תרתי, והכא חדא הוא דהואי, ואכשריה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:3:1.english: In accordance with his teaching - That we require two [conditions to disqualify it], and here there was [only] one, and he declared it valid.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:4:1.hebrew: היכא דמזבני כיתנא - דשיירות מצויות שם לבא ולקנות. ואהדריה משום דלא הוחזקו שני יוסף בן שמעון בעיר שנכתב בה, ולא חיישינן לומר יש עיר אחרת ששמה כזו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:4:1.english: Where they sell flax - For caravans are common there to come and buy. And [Rabbah] returned it because two [men named] Yosef ben Shimon were not established [to live] in the city in which it was written, and we are not concerned to say [that] there is another city whose name is like this [one].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:5:1.hebrew: ואיכא דאמרי היכא דתרו כיתנא - במי המשרה, שם נמצא הגט. ומאי "כשמעתיה"? שהוחזקו שני יוסף בן שמעון באותה עיר שנכתב בה, ואכשריה, דבמקום שנמצא בו לא היו שיירות מצויות:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 18b:5:1.english: And there are those who say, where they soak flax - In the soaking water — there the bill of divorce was found. And what is [the meaning of] "in accordance with his teaching"? That two [men named] Yosef ben Shimon were established [to live] in that city in which it was written, yet he ruled it valid, because in the place where it was found, caravans were not common.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 18b:15:1.hebrew: מעולם לא חתמנו אלא על גט אחד כו' - ואומר הבעל שהוא אותו יוסף. וא"ת: והלא כשאין העדים אומרים כן, אינו נאמן לומר שהוא שלו, אלא אנו חוששין שמא מאחר נפל; ועתה שעדים אומרים שלא חתמו אלא על גט אחד של יוסף בן שמעון, למה יהא נאמן? ליחוש שמא לאחר חתמו ולא לזה! וי"ל: דאף כי אין עדים, מה שאינו נאמן אע"ג שאומר "מכיר אני שהוא שלי" — לפי שמספק אומר שהוא שלו, לפי שסבור שלא איבד אחר גט רק הוא, לכך אומר שהוא שלו אע"פ שאינו מכיר. אבל כשעדים אומרים שלא חתמו רק על גט אחד של יוסף בן שמעון, במזיד לא ישקר אם חתמו לאחר לומר שלא חתמו, דאינו חשוד לקלקלה, כמו שנאמן לומר "גרשתיה". ואית ספרים דגרסי: "אלא על גט אחד של יוסף בן שמעון זה" — אתי שפיר טפי. וצריך לומר שלא ראו עדים החתימה, דאי ראו החתימה שהיא שלהם, א"כ הוה ליה למימר: "מהו דתימא דלמא אתרמאי עדים כעדים וחתימה כחתימה":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 18b:15:1.english: "We have never signed [a bill of divorce] other than one [of Yosef ben Shimon]" etc. - And the husband says that he is that Yosef [ben Shimon]. And if you ask: When the witnesses do not say this, is he not disbelieved when he says that it is his, rather we are concerned lest it fell from another [man with the same name]; so now that witnesses say that they only signed one bill of divorce of Yosef ben Shimon, why should he be believed? Let us be concerned lest they signed [it] for another [Yosef ben Shimon] and not for this one! And one can answer: Even when there are no witnesses, the reason he is not believed even though he says, "I recognize that it is mine," is because he says it is his out of uncertainty — since he assumes that no one else lost a bill of divorce except him, therefore he says that it is his even though he does not [truly] recognize [it]. However, when witnesses say that they only signed one bill of divorce of Yosef ben Shimon, [the husband] would not deliberately lie — if they had signed [it] for another [man] — to claim that they did not sign [for another], for he is not suspected of ruining her [status], just as he is believed to say, "I divorced her." And there are texts that read: "other than one bill of divorce of this Yosef ben Shimon" — [which] works out even better. And it must be said that the witnesses did not see the signature [on the found bill of divorce], for if they saw the signature [and recognized] that it was theirs, if so, [the Gemara] should have said: "Lest you say that perhaps witnesses coincided with witnesses [of the same name], and signature [handwriting] with signature [handwriting]."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 18b:1:1.hebrew: חיישינן לשני שוירי - וא"ת: א"כ לרב הונא היאך יגרש כל אדם את אשתו לר"מ, דאינו מוכיח מתוכו כיון דחיישינן לשני שוירי? וי"ל: כיון דלא הוחזקו הוי שפיר מוכיח מתוכו, ומ"מ כשנפל חיישינן:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 18b:1:1.english: We are concerned about two [cities named] Sheviri - And if you ask: If so, according to Rav Huna, how can any man divorce his wife according to Rabbi Meir, since [the bill of divorce] is not self-evident from within itself, as we are concerned about two [cities named] Sheviri? And one can answer: Since [two such cities] have not been established [to exist], it is indeed [considered] self-evident from within itself; and nevertheless, when it has fallen, we are concerned:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 18b:1:2.hebrew: נפק דק ואשכח כל מעשה ב"ד הרי זה יחזיר - פרש"י דההוא גיטא הוה כתיב ביה הנפק, ופשיט שפיר ממתני' דמעשה ב"ד יחזיר. אך מה שפירש כשנפל מן השליח — קשה, דא"כ מה מועיל ההנפק כיון שלא בא ליד האשה עדיין? דאם יש לחוש לנמלך בלא הנפק, הכי נמי יש לחוש להנפק; ותו, דבעל לא מקיים גיטא. וי"ל דאי כתיב ביה הנפק, מיירי שנפל מן האשה, ושואלת אותו האשה ואומרת שהוא שלה, וקא פשיט דיחזיר ולא חיישינן שמא משקרת ומאשה אחרת נפל, אע"ג דהשיירות מצויות, כיון דלא הוחזקו — כמו במעשה ב"ד דיחזיר ואע"ג דאשתכח בב"ד שהשיירות מצויות, ולא חיישינן שמא מאחר נפל, כיון דלא הוחזקו. ואי מיירי שהשליח שואלו לגרש את האשה, י"ל דלא כתיב בו הנפק. ומוכיח נמי שפיר: כיון דבמעשה ב"ד יחזיר, דלא חיישינן לנמלך — דכיון שכתוב בו הנפק, ודאי נעשה הלואה, דלוה לא מקיים שטרא, כדאמרינן לקמן בפרקין (בבא מציעא דף כ:) — ולא חיישינן נמי שמא מאחר נפל, אע"ג דהשיירות מצויות, כיון דלא הוחזקו; בההיא גיטא נמי דאשתכח, שהשליח שואל הגט, ולא שייך למימר נמלך כיון שהגט ביד השליח, דאין יכול לבטל הגט שלא בפני השליח, ולא ניחוש כמו כן שמא מאחר נפל, אף על גב דהשיירות מצויות, כיון דלא הוחזקו. וא"ת: אביי, דאמר פ' האשה שהלכה (יבמות דף קטו: ושם) דחיישינן לתרי יצחק אפי' לא הוחזקו, תקשי ליה ממתניתין דכל מעשה ב"ד הרי זה יחזיר! וי"ל דמוקי לה דאשתכח חוץ לב"ד שאין השיירות מצויות, כר' זירא; אבל לגבי תרי יצחק לא שייך לפלוגי בין מצויות לשאין מצויות, דלעולם יש להסתפק ביצחק מעיר אחרת כמו מעיר זאת. אי נמי, מוקי מתני' דאשתכח בב"ד, ואפי' הכי לא חיישינן לאחר, כיון שזה האיש שואל גט וידעינן שאבד גט ואין אנו מכירין אחר — אין לחוש שמאחר נפל ונפל ממנו כמו כן כאן; אבל התם אין אנו יודעים איזה יצחק מת, אם מעיר זאת או מעיר אחרת:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 18b:1:2.english: "He went out, examined [it], and discovered ... any court enactment, one must return [it]" - Rashi explained that on that bill of divorce a court authentication (hanpak) was written, and [Rabbah] validly resolves [the question] from the Mishnah that a court enactment must be returned. However, what [Rashi] explained — that [the case is] when it fell from the agent — is difficult: for if so, what does the hanpak accomplish, since it has not yet reached the woman's hand? For if one must be concerned that [the husband] reconsidered without a hanpak, so too one must be concerned [even] with a hanpak; and furthermore, a husband does not authenticate a bill of divorce. And one can answer that if a hanpak is written on it, [the Gemara] is dealing with [a case] where it fell from the woman, and the woman requests it and says that it is hers, and [Rabbah] resolves that one must return [it] and we are not concerned that perhaps she is lying and it fell from another woman — even though caravans are common — since [two people of the same name] have not been established [to live there], just like in [the case of] a court enactment, which one must return even though it was found in the courthouse where caravans are common, and we are not concerned that perhaps it fell from another, since they have not been established. And if [the Gemara] is dealing with [a case] where the agent requests it to divorce the woman, one can say that a hanpak is not written on it. And [Rabbah] also proves [this] well: since in [the case of] a court enactment one must return [it], as we are not concerned that [the borrower] reconsidered — for since a hanpak is written on it, the loan was certainly executed, because a borrower does not authenticate a note, as we say later in our chapter (Bava Metzia 20b) — and we are also not concerned that perhaps it fell from another, even though caravans are common, since they have not been established; so too with that bill of divorce that was found, where the agent requests the bill of divorce, and it is not relevant to say [the husband] reconsidered since the bill of divorce is in the agent's hand, for he cannot nullify the bill of divorce not in the presence of the agent, and similarly we should not be concerned that perhaps it fell from another, even though caravans are common, since they have not been established. And if you say: Abaye, who says in the chapter HaIsha SheHalkha (Yevamot 115b and there) that we are concerned about two [men named] Yitzḥak even when they have not been established — let [the question] be difficult for him from the Mishnah of "any court enactment, one must return [it]"! One can answer that he establishes it [as referring to a case] where it was found outside the courthouse where caravans are not common, in accordance with Rabbi Zeira; however, regarding two [men named] Yitzḥak, it is not relevant to distinguish between [places where caravans are] common and [places where they are] not common, for one must always be in doubt about a Yitzḥak from another city just as [about one] from this city. Alternatively, he establishes the Mishnah [as referring to a case] where it was found in the courthouse, and even so we are not concerned about another [person], since this man is requesting a bill of divorce and we know that a bill of divorce was lost and we do not know of another [person of that name], there is no concern that perhaps it fell from another, and similarly here [with a bill of divorce] it fell from him; however, there [in Yevamot], we do not know which Yitzḥak died, whether from this city or from another city.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 18b:6:1.hebrew: אין הבעל מודה לא יחזיר - אע"ג דנאמנת לומר גרשתני (גיטין דף סד:), הכא אינה נאמנת, דמעיזה פניה כיון דהגט מסייעה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 18b:6:1.english: "[If] the husband does not admit [to it], he may not return [it]" - Even though [a woman] is believed to say, "You divorced me" (Gittin 64b), here she is not believed, for she acts brazenly [and would lie], since the bill of divorce supports her.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 18b:7:1.hebrew: ואפילו לזמן מרובה - תימה: כיון שמודה שממנה נפל וכבר גירשה, אמאי הוה לן למימר דלא יחזיר? כיון דנאמן לומר "גרשתיה", כדאמר פרק יש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קלד:), אפילו נפל מאחר נחזיר לה לראיה בעלמא. וי"ל: דנאמן לומר "גרשתיה" ותהא מגורשת מכאן ולהבא, הואיל ובידו לגרשה; אבל הכא, שאומר שכבר גרשה מזמן הכתוב בגט, כמו שאינו נאמן למפרע — כך אינו נאמן להבא. ו"יחזיר לאשה" דקתני — היינו בעדים, ותתגרש בו בחזרה זו, ולא חיישינן שמא מאחר נפל, ואפילו לזמן מרובה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 18b:7:1.english: And even after a long time - This is astonishing: since he admits that it fell from her and [that] he already divorced her, why would we have thought to say that [the finder] should not return [it]? Since he is believed to say, "I divorced her," as it says in the chapter [entitled] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 134b), even if it fell from another [person], we should return [it] to her merely as proof [of her divorce]. And it can be answered: he is believed to say, "I divorced her," [so] that she is divorced from now onward, since it is in his power to divorce her; however, here, where he says that he already divorced her from the date written in the bill of divorce, just as he is not believed retroactively — so too he is not believed prospectively. And [the ruling] "he must return [it] to the wife" that [the baraita] teaches — that means in [the presence of] witnesses, so that she becomes divorced with it through this returning, and we are not concerned lest it fell from another [person], even after a long time.
